slides.text: To survive Thanksgiving without my family asking why I’m still single at thirty-four, I hired an off-Broadway actor named Devon for three hundred dollars to pose as my fiancé, a pediatric neurosurgeon who rescues greyhounds. Everything was going brilliantly during appetizers—until my younger sister arrived with her 'new boyfriend,' a rugged firefighter who locked eyes with Devon and whispered, 'Wait. Kevin from the Chekhov audition?'

Before either of them could recover, my recently widowed grandmother walked in on the arm of a silver-haired 'retired ambassador' who gasped and pointed at both men. 'Are you guys booked through Rent-A-Beau Local 402?! How much is she paying you?' Within ninety seconds, all three actors were comparing day rates over the cranberry sauce while my mother quietly tried to slip her own 'new tennis coach' out the back door.

It turned out not a single woman in my bloodline had brought a real human partner since 2019. By the time the turkey came out, the four actors had unionized at the dining table, demanding time-and-a-half hazard pay if my Uncle Gary brought up crypto. We paid the surcharge. Honestly, it was the most peaceful Thanksgiving we've ever had, and we've already renewed their contracts for Christmas.
